question: A can complete a piece of work in 66 days. B is 45% less efficient than A. C is 50% more efficient than B. If B and C work together for 24 days, then A alone will complete the remaining work in:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Efficiency ratio of A : B : C = 100 : 55 : 82.5 = 40 : 22 : 33.

Total work = Efficiency of A × Time = 40 × 66 = 2640 units.

Work done by B and C in 24 days = (22 + 33) × 24 = 1320 units.

Remaining work = 2640 − 1320 = 1320 units.

Time for A to complete remaining work = 1320 ÷ 40 = 33 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 33 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

A can complete the work in 66 days.

B is 45% less efficient than A.

C is 50% more efficient than B.

B and C work together for 24 days.

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Efficiency × Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the efficiency of A = 100 units/day.

⇒ Efficiency of B = 100 − 45% of 100 = 55 units/day.

⇒ Efficiency of C = 55 + 50% of 55 = 82.5 units/day.

⇒ Simplifying the ratio of efficiencies A : B : C = 100 : 55 : 82.5 = 40 : 22 : 33.

⇒ Total work = 40 × 66 = 2640 units.

⇒ Time taken by B = 2640 ÷ 22 = 120 days.

⇒ Time taken by C = 2640 ÷ 33 = 80 days.

⇒ Combined efficiency of B and C = 22 + 33 = 55 units/day.

⇒ Work done by B and C in 24 days = 55 × 24 = 1320 units.

⇒ Remaining work = 2640 − 1320 = 1320 units.

⇒ Time taken by A to complete remaining work = 1320 ÷ 40 = 33 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 33 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns

Works on the same concept as Time & Work. Inlet pipes have positive efficiency, and outlet pipes have negative efficiency.

Work and Wages

Wages are distributed in direct proportion to the actual amount of work done by each individual. If they work for the exact same number of days, wages are directly distributed in the ratio of their efficiencies.

Alternate Day Work

When people work on alternate days, find the total work done in one cycle (e.g., 2 days for 2 people) and determine how many complete cycles fit into the total work before solving for the remaining individual days.
